_status: needs_validation. Field names, condition types and enum values were checked on 2026-11-24 against Akamai's Application Security API reference (techdocs.akamai.com, 'Create a custom rule' and 'Create a rate policy'). Nothing here has been imported into an Akamai configuration. Two things the reference leaves open: it documents valueWildcard for requestHeaderMatch only, although its own example sets it on cookie, query and extension conditions, and its argsPostMatch example carries no wildcard flag at all - so validate the pathMatch, uriQueryMatch and argsPostMatch rules in alert before trusting them. The same caution applies to name '*' with nameWildcard on uriQueryMatch and argsPostMatch (documented for requestHeaderMatch only: if it is not honoured those rules look for a parameter literally named '*' and never match), and to valueRecursive on the W-AGT-008 filenameMatch (documented, default not stated; set true here so files below the root folder match). Whether pathMatch sees the path as sent or normalized is not documented on the public pages, so the encoded and ';parameter' forms the other two files were tested against are unverified here.
_usage: Each entry under customRules has a recommended action and a rule body. POST the rule body, then set the action per security policy. operation AND requires every condition; values inside one condition are ORed. Start every rule in alert. The structured builder matches ? and * wildcards, not regular expressions, so W-AGT-007, W-AGT-008 and W-AGT-011 are approximations of the regex versions in the other files. Custom rules are active for 30 days by default: set effectiveTimePeriod or renew them.
_network_list: W-AGT-010: load blocklist-ipv4.txt as a Network List and deny it in IP/Geo Firewall. No custom rule needed.
_tls_fingerprint: The reference lists a clientTlsFingerprintMatch condition and a tls-fingerprint rate-policy client identifier. The three JA4 values in iocs.csv are deliberately not shipped as a rule: they identify an HTTP client library seen on a researcher's instance. Use them in an alert-only rule of your own if you want the signal.
_not_expressible: W-AGT-009 (DTD in an XML body) and W-AGT-012 (upload filename traversal) are not shipped as custom rules. Akamai's condition-type list names argsPostJSONMatch, argsPostJSONNamesMatch and argsPostXMLMatch, but the type enum on the 'Create a custom rule' page omits all three, so a rule using them could not be checked against the schema; and none of them exposes a multipart filename or a DTD. On Akamai these two are covered by the Adaptive Security Engine attack groups (keep them in deny) rather than by a custom rule here.
_rate_policy_notes: clientIdentifier is deprecated but still listed as required, so both it and clientIdentifiers are set; tls-fingerprint keeps counting one client as it rotates addresses. penaltyBoxDuration applies only with counterType region_aggregated. W-AGT-034 (repeat WAF violators) is not a rate policy on Akamai: turn on the security policy's penalty box instead. Thresholds are hits per SECOND and the minimum is 1: averageThreshold 1 means about 120 matching requests in two minutes, and burstThreshold N means N a second for five seconds. A rate policy therefore cannot express the low-and-slow thresholds the README gives for the other platforms (more than 10 failed logins in 5 minutes, more than 3 sign-ups an hour): W-AGT-031 and W-AGT-032 here catch only the machine-speed end of those behaviours. Use Account Protector or Bot Manager for the slow end.

rule.name: W-AGT-001 agent framework user-agent
rule.description: User-agents compiled into ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI and HexStrike-AI. Mirrors ua-block.txt.

rule.name: W-AGT-001b ARTEX named in the user-agent
rule.description: The framework's own name at the start of a word in the User-Agent. F5 Labs (2026-11-23) lists 46 user-agents it tied to ARTEX, made up by the agent per task; 44 carry the name. Alert, not deny: the wildcard builder can say 'at the start of the header, after a space or after an opening bracket' but cannot say what may follow, so this also matches a product such as ArtExpo. The regex versions in the other files can, and deny.

rule.name: W-AGT-003 agent-adjacent user-agent
rule.description: Tools with legitimate users (Norma agent library, ffuf, PentAGI installer), the low-confidence ReconProbe client, and user-agents that declare themselves authorized, read-only or pentest (Bitrise and Barracuda incidents, Wiz's Black October list), which a real tester sends too. Context only, never deny. Mirrors ua-alert.txt, plus norma/ at the start of the header at any version (Microsoft 2026-11-25 lists norma/*).

rule.name: W-AGT-004a agent canary path
rule.description: Baseline-404 probes recorded by Wiz, Unit 42 and Datadog, and the _i<counter>_probe_missing SSRF canary path of the Bitrise incident (Wiz's Black October list; ? is one character, so the counter is approximated as two to seven characters).

rule.name: W-AGT-004b agent canary in query string
rule.description: Canary usernames, placeholder emails, junk OAuth state, metadata-service SSRF and the _i<counter>_probe_missing SSRF canary path (sent as a URL inside a parameter) in the query string.

rule.name: W-AGT-004c agent canary in POST body
rule.description: Same strings in form arguments: login, sign-up and account-recovery endpoints, and the _i<counter>_probe_missing SSRF canary path sent as a URL inside a form field.

rule.name: W-AGT-005 unsigned JWT in Authorization
rule.description: JWT whose header is alg none, in three casings and with typ first. Base64 is case-sensitive.

rule.name: W-AGT-006 ARTEX-tagged SQL injection probe
rule.description: S-RM: injection strings tagged with the framework name. Query string; duplicate with argsPostMatch for bodies.

rule.name: W-AGT-007 agent probe-account identity
rule.description: Okta: i<intent>probe<10-digit unix time>@, with the intent counter two to seven digits (Wiz 2026-11-25 saw i49 to i808807). Wildcard approximation (? is one character); current timestamps start with 1.

rule.name: W-AGT-008 agent task-artifact script name
rule.description: S-RM: i<number>.<script ext>, three to seven characters after the i, the first of them a digit (Wiz 2026-11-25 saw the counter from i49 to i808807; two-digit names are left out of this rule as likelier to be real files). ? matches any character, so only the first character after the i is held to a digit: i4abc.php would still match, which is looser than the regex elsewhere, so alert first. Before 2026-11-28 the values were i??? to i???????, which also matched index.php, info.php, install.php and include.php. The second shape (GTIG: cl1217.jsp, f1219a.jsp) needs a regex and is not expressible here.

rule.name: W-AGT-020 source map, API spec or Swagger UI requested
rule.description: Exposure reduction. Move to deny (with an internal network-list exception) once nothing public depends on these.

rule.name: W-AGT-011 shell command in User-Agent
rule.description: Microsoft 2026-11-05: exploitation attempts by shell commands embedded in a user agent. Wildcard approximation of the regex in the other files.

rule.name: W-AGT-013 isCliRequest header present
rule.description: Amazon: authentication bypass used against One API family LLM gateways. Matters only in front of such a gateway.

rule.name: W-AGT-014a path traversal in path
rule.description: Traversal sequences in the path, plain and encoded. The Adaptive Security Engine local-file-inclusion group covers this class and should stay in deny; this custom rule is a second line. Whether the edge shows a custom rule the path before or after normalization is not stated in the API reference, so validate in alert.

rule.name: W-AGT-014b path traversal in query string
rule.description: Amazon 2026-11-20: Cairn agents found traversal in a filename parameter in about 11 minutes.

rule.name: W-AGT-021a secret file requested
rule.description: Dotenv files and git metadata are never served to anyone.

rule.name: W-AGT-021b management endpoint to external client
rule.description: Spring Boot Actuator and Go pprof. The health endpoint is excluded for load balancers. Add an ipMatch or clientListMatch condition with positiveMatch false for your own ranges before moving to deny. The health exemption is an explicit list (health, health/liveness, health/readiness): a wildcard tail would also exempt /actuator/health/..;/env, which Tomcat and Spring serve as /actuator/env. Add your own health groups by name.

rule.name: W-AGT-021c management endpoint reached through the health exemption
rule.description: W-AGT-021b exempts paths ending in /actuator/health. A path with a second /actuator segment before that ending (for example /actuator/jolokia/exec/x/actuator/health) is not the health endpoint; refuse it. Add the same ipMatch or clientListMatch condition you add to W-AGT-021b.

policy.name: W-AGT-030 error-rate enumeration
policy.description: Clients drawing not-found or denied responses at machine speed. Per the reference, averageThreshold is allowed hits per second during any two-minute interval and burstThreshold is hits per second during any five-second interval; derive yours from a baseline.

policy.name: W-AGT-031 source-centric login failures
policy.description: Failed logins per client across any number of usernames. Set path values to your login and token endpoints. Fires at about one failure a second sustained (the lowest rate a rate policy can express), not at the 10-in-5-minutes threshold used on the other platforms.

policy.name: W-AGT-032 self-registration rate
policy.description: Sign-up posts per client. Okta saw thousands of fraudulent self-service registrations. Set path values to your sign-up endpoints. Fires at about one sign-up a second sustained (the lowest rate a rate policy can express), not at the 3-an-hour threshold used on the other platforms.

policy.name: W-AGT-033 OAuth authorize probing
policy.description: Unit 42 and Okta: unregistered redirect URIs tried across many client IDs. Rate the authorize endpoint's error responses per client.
